scheme_name: “Exposure Tour for the Coir Artisans” Component of the "Development of Coir" Scheme
description:
The "Exposure Tour for the Coir Artisans" is a significant component of the broader "Development of Coir" scheme initiated by the Government of India. 

The "Development of Coir" scheme was launched in 2014. 

This scheme aims to enhance the production and productivity of coir and coir products. 

The scheme also focuses on improving the livelihoods of coir artisans and workers. 

The exposure tour component specifically aims to provide coir artisans with opportunities to learn from successful coir production units. 

The objective is to enhance their skills and knowledge about modern coir processing techniques. 

The exposure tour is designed to facilitate the exchange of ideas and best practices among artisans. 

It also aims to promote innovation in coir production and design. 

The target is to conduct exposure tours for at least 1,000 coir artisans annually. 

These tours are expected to cover various regions known for coir production. 

The artisans are exposed to advanced technologies and practices in coir processing. 

This helps them improve the quality of their products. 

The financial assistance provided under this component is substantial. 

Each exposure tour can cost around ₹50,000. 

The government provides a subsidy of 50% of the total cost. 

This means that artisans can receive up to ₹25,000 for participating in these tours. 

The eligibility criteria for artisans to participate in the exposure tours are specific. 

Artisans must be registered under the Coir Board. 

They must also have at least one year of experience in coir production. 

The age limit for participating artisans is set at a minimum of 18 years. 

There is no upper age limit specified. 

Artisans must also belong to a cooperative society or a self-help group. 

The application process for the exposure tour is straightforward. 

Interested artisans must fill out an application form available on the Coir Board's official website. 

They need to submit proof of their registration with the Coir Board. 

Additionally, they must provide evidence of their experience in coir production. 

The application must also include a recommendation from their cooperative society or self-help group. 

Once the application is submitted, it is reviewed by the Coir Board. 

Successful applicants are notified about their selection for the exposure tour. 

The tours are organized at least twice a year. 

The specific dates for the tours are announced by the Coir Board in advance. 

Participants are provided with travel allowances and accommodation during the tour. 

The tours typically last for about 7 to 10 days. 

During the tours, artisans visit successful coir production units. 

They also attend workshops and training sessions conducted by experts. 

The exposure tours have shown significant positive outcomes. 

Artisans report improved skills and knowledge after participating. 

Many artisans have successfully adopted new techniques learned during the tours. 

This has led to increased productivity and better quality products. 

The Coir Board monitors the outcomes of these exposure tours. 

They collect feedback from participants to assess the impact. 

The exposure tour component is implemented by the Coir Board of India. 

The Coir Board was established in 1953. 

It operates under the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises. 

The headquarters of the Coir Board is located in Kochi, Kerala. 

The Coir Board also has several regional offices across India. 

Artisans can contact the Coir Board for more information about the exposure tours. 

The contact details for the Coir Board are available on their official website. 

The website also provides updates on upcoming tours and application deadlines. 

The exposure tour initiative aligns with the government's broader goals of skill development. 

It supports the "Make in India" initiative by promoting indigenous industries. 

The coir industry is a significant source of employment in coastal areas. 

It provides livelihoods to over 7 lakh artisans across India. 

The exposure tours are part of a larger effort to modernize the coir sector. 

The government aims to increase the export of coir products. 

The export target for coir products is set at ₹2,500 crores by 2025. 

The exposure tours contribute to achieving this target by enhancing product quality. 

The tours also aim to foster entrepreneurship among coir artisans. 

By learning about successful business models, artisans can start their own ventures. 

The Coir Board also provides additional support to artisans post-tour. 

This includes access to marketing platforms and financial assistance for new projects. 

The overall impact of the exposure tours is significant for the coir sector. 

They play a crucial role in empowering artisans and improving their economic conditions. 

The exposure tours have become a vital part of the Development of Coir scheme. 

They are instrumental in promoting sustainable practices in coir production. 

The initiative has received positive feedback from participants and stakeholders. 

Artisans express gratitude for the opportunity to learn and grow. 

The Coir Board continues to refine and improve the exposure tour program. 

This ensures that it meets the evolving needs of coir artisans across India. 

The exposure tour for coir artisans is a prime example of targeted welfare initiatives. 

It highlights the government's commitment to supporting traditional industries. 

The scheme aims to uplift the coir community and ensure their sustainable development. 

In conclusion, the "Exposure Tour for the Coir Artisans" component of the "Development of Coir" scheme is a well-structured initiative. 

It provides valuable opportunities for skill enhancement and knowledge transfer. 

The program is designed to empower artisans and improve their livelihoods. 

Through this initiative, the government aims to strengthen the coir industry in India. 

The focus on innovation and best practices is crucial for the sector's growth. 

The exposure tours are a testament to the government's dedication to artisan welfare. 

They represent a significant step towards the modernization of traditional crafts. 

The initiative is expected to yield long-term benefits for the coir artisans and the industry as a whole.
